problems.form_value: n_randomized 387, arms 56, 69, 67, 53, 74, 68, recorded as counts at randomization. Exclusions: 'The paper does not say how many, or whether the 387 it gives as the result of random allocation (p. 3; Table 1, p. 4) is counted before or after that removal.'
problems.source_says: The attention check came at the end of the study, after allocation (Figure 1), and failures were 'removed from the sample'. All 387 enter the H2 ANOVA (F (5, 381)) and Table 3 (prime creativity, CSE, CPI N = 387), and the Table 1 arm sizes reproduce that ANOVA (error df 381, grand mean 3.42, SD 1.32, eta squared 0.485). So the 387 and the arm sizes count the people kept after the removal. The form calls the timing unknown, but the paper's own counts settle it. The number randomized is 387 plus an unreported number of failures (possibly zero). The paper never prints it, so n_randomized should be null, or 387 labeled as allocated and retained.
problems.quote: At the conclusion of the study, participants were also asked to complete an attention check. ... Participants who selected the incorrect answer were removed from the sample.
problems.locator: p. 4, Section 3.4 and Figure 1 (Attn Check is the last step); p. 3, Section 3.1 and p. 4, Table 1 ('The random allocation to priming conditions resulted in the following groups'); p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Section 4.2

problems.source_says: The arm means and SDs come from the 381 people with a DAT score. The only per-arm ns printed are the Table 1 counts, which sum to 387. The analyzed ns that go with the means are printed nowhere, and the 6 missing scores can sit in any arm: dropping 6 people from different arms moves the reproduced F between 5.90 and 6.44. The form's 'reported' text says the ns are allocation counts, but the tag implies that the matching analyzed ns exist. Minor.
problems.quote: There was a statistically significant difference in DAT scores for the six priming condition groups: F (5, 375) = 6.39, p < 0.001.
problems.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1 and Table 3 (DAT score N = 381); p. 6, Section 4.1; p. 4, Table 1

confirmed.statement: The paper reports one randomized study: individuals were allocated at random to one of six priming conditions after the covariates. There is no pilot, no second experiment, no flow diagram with counts, and no appendix sample.
confirmed.quote: Participants responded to a set of demographic questions and a suite of personality, creativity, and AI covariates before being randomly allocated to one of six priming conditions.
confirmed.locator: p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 4, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; pp. 1-10 read in full

confirmed.statement: Table 1 matches the form's arm sizes: HuLo 56, HuTy 69, HuHi 67, ChLo 53, ChTy 74, ChHi 68, total 387 (the sum checks). The arm word lists match Table 2, and the 'a student' and 'ChatGPT' labels match Section 3.3.
confirmed.quote: The random allocation to priming conditions resulted in the following groups (Table 1).
confirmed.locator: p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 4, Tables 1 and 2 and Section 3.3

confirmed.statement: The counts are people. The gender counts sum to 387 (107 + 273 + 6 + 1). The race percentages fit 387 people exactly when cut to two decimals (267, 16, 46, 16, 1, 39), and no other total from 300 to 499 fits.
confirmed.quote: Of the 387 participants, 107 identified as male, 273 identified as female, and 6 identified as non-binary, fluid, or transgender, while a single participant declined to respond.

confirmed.statement: 381 people were analyzed on the DAT, one score each. Table 3 gives DAT score N = 381, and the one-way between-groups ANOVA's error df (375) plus 6 groups gives 381. The form's study-level n_analyzed = 381 is right.

Table 1's arm sizes reproduce the full-sample analyses. With them, the H2 arm means and SDs give error df 381, grand mean 3.42, SD 1.32, eta squared 0.485, and F 71.7 (printed: F (5, 381) = 71.90, eta squared 0.48; the gap fits two-decimal rounding of the SDs). The H1 arm means give a grand mean near 80.25 and an SD of 6.30, as in Table 3.
confirmed.quote: There was a statistically significant difference in perceived response creativity scores for the six priming condition groups: F (5, 381) = 71.90, p < 0.001.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Table 1; p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Sections 4.1 and 4.2

confirmed.statement: Per-arm analyzed DAT counts are printed nowhere, so arms[].n_analyzed = null is right. The paper does not explain the 6 missing DAT scores (387 to 381).
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Section 4.1 and Figure 2 (95 percent CI bars, no ns)

confirmed.statement: The form's other exclusion arithmetic is right. The H3 regression df (F (1, 376) at step 1 to F (6, 371) at step 5) imply 378 people at every step, while Table 3 gives 'Total (valid)' N = 376. Table 3 also gives N = 384 for Openness and for Propensity to trust AI, which matters only for the regression.
confirmed.quote: Openness was entered at step 1, with the model significantly predicting creativity (DAT), F (1, 376) = 19.87, p < 0.001

confirmed.statement: No sample overlap. The paper has one study and cites no other report of these data. The N = 102 from Cropley (2023) is a set of ChatGPT responses used to set the prime levels, not people. No other record in candidates.json or the forms folder reports this sample (c164 and c272 checked; no other form mentions Nebraska or IRB 0223-23-EX), and a web search on 5 October 2026 found no other paper that uses it.
confirmed.quote: The creativity level of the list of nouns was determined from a sample (Cropley 2023) of ChatGPT responses (N = 102)
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 3.3; p. 9, Ethics Statement; candidates.json; forms folder

confirmed.statement: Population and country are right: students at one urban university in the US Midwest.
confirmed.quote: First, this research was conducted using a university student sample, which may not be representative of the population at large.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds by a wide margin: one randomized study with 381 people analyzed, and the smallest arm (ChLo) has 53 people.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Table 1; p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Section 4.1

summary: One randomized study analyzed 381 students on the DAT, one score each (Table 3; F (5, 375)), and the arm sizes match Table 1, so criterion 2 holds by a wide margin. The coding is refuted on details: attention-check failures were removed after allocation and all 387 enter the H2 ANOVA, so 387 and the Table 1 arm sizes count the people kept, not the people randomized (a number the paper never prints), and the contrasts' 'arm_means_sds_ns' tag pairs 381-person means with 387-person counts.
